recent_articles.title: Unlike Centre, Sindh announces four Eid holidays - Pakistan - DAWN.COM

recent_articles.title: Picked wrong Melody? Parle Industries shares hit 5% upper circuit for 3rd day - The Economic Times

recent_articles.title: Babar, Naseem recalled as PCB announces 16-member squad for Australia ODIs - Sport - DAWN.COM

recent_articles.title: Ladakh leaders to meet Home Ministry officials on May 22, Sonam Wangchuk part of delegation - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: A delegation from Ladakh, including climate activist **Sonam Wangchuk**, is meeting with **Union Home Ministry** officials on Friday to discuss demands for constitutional safeguards such as Statehood and inclusion under the Sixth Schedule of the Constitution. recent_articles.title: Bihar midday meal incident: HC asks whether NGO can continue providing meals - The Hindu

The court questioned whether the NGO supplying meals to over 1,800 students should continue operations during the probe and raised concerns about discrepancies in food sample collection and testing.  The court directed officials to file affidavits explaining the processes involved. The matter will be heard again on June 2nd.

recent_articles.title: Seems PTI will now have to 'resort to agitation', says MNA after party leaders yet again denied meeting with Imran - Pakistan - DAWN.COM

recent_articles.title: Modi, Shah are traitors who are attacking the Constitution, says Rahul at Rae Bareli meet - The Hindu

recent_articles.title: Fatima Sana to lead women’s side as PCB announces squad for T20 World Cup, Ireland tri-series - Sport - DAWN.COM

recent_articles.title: LHC upholds widows’ right to interest on delayed insurance payments - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
recent_articles.sentiment_target: State Life Insurance Corporation of Pakistan
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The **Lahore High Court** upheld the right of widows and legal heirs of deceased policyholders to receive statutory interest on delayed group insurance payments from **State Life Insurance Corporation of Pakistan**. The court rejected the corporation's arguments that Section 47B of the Insurance Act, 1938 was no longer enforceable due to Islamic injunctions. Justice Raheel Kamran dismissed all four appeals filed by the corporation and ordered the payment of statutory interest at a rate five percent higher than the prevailing bank rate from the date of death of each insured person until realization of the amount.  The court also rejected objections regarding limitation and maintainability, noting that the claimants had pursued remedies in good faith despite confusion regarding the proper legal forum for insurance disputes.

recent_articles.title: Lawmakers decry slow internet in National Assembly, across country - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
recent_articles.rephrased_article: Several members of the **National Assembly** raised concerns about slow internet connectivity affecting the paperless working environment in parliament.  **Deputy Speaker Ghulam Mustafa Shah** directed authorities to address the issue, while **Federal Information Technology and Telecom Minister Shaza Fatima Khawaja** assured them that the spectrum auction would improve internet facilities. **Khawaja** also addressed concerns over digital harassment, online fraud, and data theft, emphasizing public awareness campaigns and collaboration with relevant institutions.

recent_articles.title: Semi-high-speed train project to turn Gujarat into manufacturing and logistics hub: Amit Shah - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Amit Shah**, **Union Home Minister**, announced that the Cabinet approved a ₹20,667 crore Ahmedabad (Sarkhej)-Dholera semi-high-speed double rail line project. The project will connect Ahmedabad to Dholera Special Investment Region and Greenfield Industrial Smart City, creating employment opportunities and positioning Gujarat as a global manufacturing hub.  **Shah** also lauded the Cabinet's decision to upgrade and modernize the Nagpur International Airport and a ₹37,500 crore scheme for surface coal and lignite gasification projects, which will contribute to India's economic growth and job creation.

recent_articles.title: Efforts on to release Kuki, Naga people held hostage in Manipur, say Ministers - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: Following the killings of four church leaders in separate ambushes, **Govindas Konthoujam**, **Losii Dikho** and other officials confirmed that at least 38 people from the Kuki and Naga communities are being held hostage by various groups.  The attacks occurred in the Kuki-dominated Kangpokpi district and the Naga-majority Noney district. The Deputy Chief Minister stated that talks were ongoing with both Kuki and Naga groups, but no resolution was reached. **Angomcha Bimol Akoijam**, a Manipur Congress MP, criticized the government's handling of the situation.  The United Naga Council (UNC) issued an ultimatum to the state government demanding the release of 20 hostages held by Kuki groups.

recent_articles.title: Indian pharma fuels Africa's 'zombie drug' and opioid crisis despite crackdown - World - DAWN.COM
recent_articles.rephrased_article: Indian pharmaceutical companies are exporting high-strength tapentadol tablets to west Africa despite a crackdown on illegal drug trade. The pills, which are often sold as tramadol and are much stronger than approved doses, are fueling a deadly opioid epidemic in the region.  The pills are being added to "zombie drugs" like kush, leading to increased addiction and health problems, including deaths from overdoses.  While India claims it has banned exports of tapentadol mixed with other drugs, shipments continue despite warnings from government officials in Nigeria, Sierra Leone, and Ghana. The Indian Drug Manufacturers’ Association defends the trade, stating that manufacturers are not responsible for what happens after their products leave their facilities. Experts warn that the lack of regulation and enforcement in Africa allows unscrupulous companies to exploit the market, leading to widespread misuse of the drug.

recent_articles.title: Karachi's Shahrah-i-Bhutto to be fully open to public by end of May: Sharjeel Memon - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Sindh** Senior Minister Sharjeel Memon announced the full opening of the Shahrah-i-Bhutto Expressway in Karachi by the end of May, a 39-kilometer high-speed corridor that will connect to the M-9 highway.  Memon stated the project is expected to save commuters at least an hour traveling into the city and improve traffic flow. **Sindh** Chief Minister Syed Murad Ali Shah had previously directed for full operationalization by April 2026. Additionally, Memon announced a new road connecting Karachi Port with the Taj Haider Bridge, which will be completed around the same time as the expressway's opening.  Memon highlighted that these projects are part of a larger effort to improve connectivity and convenience in **Karachi**.

recent_articles.title: Trump taps David Venturella, former private prison executive, to lead ICE | Donald Trump News | Al Jazeera

recent_articles.title: IHC rules high courts can assume jurisdiction in cases of promotion assessments - Pakistan - DAWN.COM

The judgment emphasized constitutional guarantees of fairness and due process, directing the Federation to reconsider promotions based on merit and fitness.

recent_articles.title: Khawaja Asif says KP now on 'same page' as Centre in fight against terrorism - Pakistan - DAWN.COM

recent_articles.title: PM austerity appeal: State leaders take steps to limit their fuel use - The Hindu

recent_articles.title: Sensing an edge, Iran 'ready to gamble' it can outlast Trump - World - DAWN.COM

recent_articles.title: Rana stars as Bangladesh win first home Test against Pakistan | Cricket News | Al Jazeera

recent_articles.title: Assam swearing-in LIVE: Himanta Biswa Sarma takes oath as Assam CM; Four MLAs sworn in as Ministers - The Hindu

recent_articles.title: Justice Aurangzeb calls for encouraging alternative dispute resolution, says SC to establish mediation centre - Pakistan - DAWN.COM

recent_articles.title: Crumbling of Awadh’s heritage amidst monument encroachments - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: A report by the Comptroller and Auditor General of India (CAG) highlights the concerning state of protected monuments in Uttar Pradesh. The report found that 31 centrally protected monuments are untraceable, with only 31 monuments having proper ownership documentation and 96 being encroached upon. Heritage activists express worry over the disappearance of these historical sites and the potential loss of Awadhi culture, which is intertwined with the architecture and traditions of these structures.  The report also found that the ASI has not been adequately enforcing existing laws and regulations, leading to inadequate planning and documentation for conservation efforts. Experts advocate for stronger legislation, including a state heritage law, to address this issue and protect these valuable cultural assets.

recent_articles.title: No one is buying Trump's Gold? Immigration attorneys say the $1 million visa scheme is 'unethical' - The Times of India

Attorneys warn that the program is risky and may lead to financial loss for applicants, citing ongoing litigation, tax complications, and potential cancellation by a future administration. Despite these concerns, some individuals are still pursuing applications, but interest in the program remains far below initial projections.

recent_articles.title: JCP likely to finalise panel to interview candidates - Pakistan - DAWN.COM

The proposals will be presented to the full commission next week, potentially leading to the finalization of new rules governing judicial appointments.

recent_articles.title: Benazir programme cuts child stunting rates: study - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
